title: Cardinality guardrails for shadow-traffic quality metrics (hard limits + sampling)
creator: Allison Grant
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
description:
Problem
Shadow traffic introduces several naturally high-cardinality fields (prompt_id, request_fingerprint, route, customer_id, experiment_id, model_version, rubric_version). If emitted naively as metric labels, this can explode time-series count in the metrics backend and trigger ingestion throttling / cardinality alerts (observed during dogfood + early beta).

This ticket implements hard limits and sampling rules for shadow-traffic metrics dimensions to protect the metrics stack while keeping the deltas actionable.

Scope
1) Enforce a strict allowlist of metric dimensions for shadow metrics (both control and shadow sides).
2) Replace high-cardinality dimensions with stable, low-cardinality substitutes (bucketing/hashing) where needed.
3) Add guardrails at two layers:
   - Client-side (emitter): prevent emitting forbidden dimensions; sample where configured.
   - Server-side (ingestion): enforce caps and drop/zero out disallowed labels defensively.
4) Provide visibility: counters for dropped labels/series + dashboards and alerts.

Non-goals
- Building a full “examples” datastore here (that lives with the shadow artifacts storage + retention work in ENG-5411).
- Supporting arbitrary user-provided dimensions (v1 must be fixed/curated).

Decisions (aligned with ADR)
Allowed metric dimensions (v1)
- tenant_tier (hosted|dedicated|private) (derived, not raw customer_id)
- region (coarsened to cloud region / DC code)
- route_group (see below)
- request_type (chat|completion|embedding|rerank)
- shadow_target_kind (model_version|quant_profile|prompt_template|routing_policy)
- metric_name (format_adherence|refusal_rate|instruction_following|...)
- rubric_version (low cardinality; pinned per experiment)
- outcome (ok|error|timeout|dropped)

Explicitly NOT allowed as metric labels
- prompt_id
- request_fingerprint
- raw route_id / route_name (unbounded)
- customer_id / tenant_id
- experiment_id (can be unbounded; use a short-lived “experiment cohort” bucket for dashboards, or query via analytics tables)
- model_id if it’s user-defined/freeform; only Redwood model slugs from curated catalog are allowed, otherwise bucket to “custom”

Route dimension strategy
- Introduced route_group dimension:
  - For Hosted: route_group = first path segment + method (e.g., “/v1/chat:POST”), plus an optional “workspace_route_hash_bucket” for internal debugging.
  - For Dedicated/Private: route_group = configured logical route key truncated to N chars, with an LRU mapping to a stable hash bucket for overflow.
- Hard cap: max distinct route_group per tenant per 1h window (default 200). Overflow goes to route_group="__other__" and increments a drop counter.

Tenant/customer dimension strategy
- No customer_id label in metrics.
- For internal debugging, emit tenant_hash_bucket (0–127) derived from HMAC(tenant_id, metrics_salt) only in internal clusters. This is disabled by default for Dedicated/Private unless explicitly enabled in tenant config (and still bucketed).

Sampling strategy
- Metrics emission sampling is separate from shadow routing sampling.
- Default sampling (v1):
  - shadow.pair.count and shadow.scoring.lag: 1.0 (always)
  - shadow.quality.delta and per-metric aggregates: 0.25 for Hosted, 1.0 for Dedicated beta (lower traffic), configurable.
- When sampling is active, we record the sampling_rate label (bounded set: {1.0, 0.5, 0.25, 0.1}) so dashboards can scale counts, and we can detect mismatched sampling across deployments.

Implementation notes
Client-side guardrails (data plane emitter)
- Added DimensionAllowlist + DimensionNormalizer in the shadow metrics emission library.
- Any forbidden dimension is dropped and counted via shadow.metrics.dropped_labels_total{label_key=...}.
- Normalization rules:
  - route -> route_group (coarsen + truncate + overflow bucket)
  - tenant_id -> tenant_hash_bucket (optional + bucketed)
  - model identifier -> model_slug if curated else “custom”

Server-side guardrails (telemetry ingestion)
- Enforced schema-level validation: reject or strip disallowed fields at ingest for shadow_* metric events.
- Added per-tenant/per-hour series limiter:
  - max_series_per_metric_per_tenant_per_hour (default 50k Hosted, 15k Dedicated, 10k Private)
  - Behavior: fail-open for user path (never block user request); for telemetry, drop series beyond limit and increment shadow.metrics.series_limited_total.
- Added backpressure integration points so when ingestion is lagging, we can further reduce sampling via dynamic config (ties into ENG-5415 mechanisms).

Observability additions
- New internal dashboards (in observability-pack):
  - Dropped labels / limited series over time (by env, tier)
  - Top offending route_groups (bounded)
  - Estimated unique series for shadow metrics (approx)
- Alerts:
  - Page: shadow.metrics.series_limited_total > threshold for 10m in prod Hosted
  - Ticket: dropped_labels_total spike (usually a client emitting bad dimensions)

Acceptance criteria
- Enabling shadow traffic at 1% routing sample on a high-volume Hosted tenant does not increase metrics backend active series by > 5% (measured via internal cardinality estimate panel).
- No metric time series contains raw prompt_id, request_fingerprint, or customer_id.
- When route cardinality exceeds caps, route_group="__other__" is used and a limiter counter increments.
- Dedicated beta tenants can opt-in to tenant_hash_bucket (bucketed) for debugging; default is off.
- Runbook references updated to include “cardinality limiter / dropped label” dashboards and how to mitigate (reduce dims, reduce sampling).

Testing / validation
- Load test: replayed ~20k QPS synthetic traffic with randomized routes/prompt_ids; verified no cardinality explosion and limiter counters behave as expected.
- Regression test: unit tests for allowlist enforcement and route_group normalization.
- Dogfood follow-up: addressed SUP-28510 by removing experiment_id label from metrics and coarsening route dimension.

Rollout plan
- Behind feature flag shadow_metrics_cardinality_guardrails (default ON in internal + beta).
- Phase 1: internal tenants only (48h), monitor dropped/limited counters.
- Phase 2: Dedicated beta cohort (3 tenants), enable tenant_hash_bucket only on request.
- Phase 3: Hosted gradual rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with SRE sign-off.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Should we support a bounded experiment_cohort label for short-lived comparisons in dashboards (e.g., “A”, “B”), sourced from rollout system, instead of forcing users into analytics tables? (proposed follow-up ENG)
- Add documentation note in quickstart about why certain fields don’t appear as filters (DevEx follow-up; link to docs PR once merged).

2026-02-02 — Allison Grant: Reviewed dashboards/alert proposals. Please add a panel that shows estimated unique series for shadow metrics (approx) so oncall can quickly confirm we’re within budget.
2026-02-07 — Caleb Johnson: Patched per-tenant/per-hour limiter and overflow route_group handling. Verified against SUP-28510 reproduction; limiter counters increment and series count stays stable.

2026-02-12 — Sean Gallagher: Oncall readiness: runbook must reference ‘dropped_labels_total’ and ‘series_limited_total’ dashboards and include mitigation steps (reduce sampling, disable tenant_hash_bucket, verify route_group mapping).
